metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Set the loser-fallback deadline below the --timeout=300 per-test guard (e.g. render locally after ~120-180s) so a crashed/slow winner degrades to local render instead of tripping pytest's timeout.
evidence: Plan: 'If the lock is held past a 600s deadline the loser renders locally rather than hang, so a crashed winner degrades to today's behaviour instead of deadlocking.'
Plan Testing/AC both pin the command to '--timeout=300'; 600s > 300s means the per-test timeout fires first
AC line: 'No single test in the module exceeds 120s under -n 3, keeping clear of the 300s hang guard'
findings.finding: The stated 600s loser-fallback deadline exceeds the --timeout=300 per-test guard, so a loser blocked on a slow/crashed winner is killed by pytest's timeout before the local-render fallback can trigger — contradicting the plan's 'degrades to today's behaviour instead of deadlocking' guarantee.
findings.location: Approach section — mutual-exclusion bullet ('If the lock is held past a 600s deadline the loser renders locally rather than hang')
scenarios: Winner worker crashes mid-render; a loser polls, never sees the artifact, and pytest's 300s timeout kills it before the 600s local-render path runs
findings.suggested_fix: Lower the poll-fallback deadline to well under 300s (e.g. 150s) so the local-render fallback fires before the per-test timeout guard, and account for the winner's own ~44s fill within that budget.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the lock-directory retire/cleanup step (who rmdir's it and when) and define loser behavior when the lock is absent but no artifact exists (re-acquire vs render local).
evidence: 'the winner renders and publishes via os.replace ... losers poll for the artifact'
'If the lock is held past a 600s deadline the loser renders locally' — covers held-lock, but not lock-released-without-artifact
No statement that the winner rmdir's the lock after publish or that losers re-acquire on a released-but-empty state
findings.finding: The lock-directory lifecycle omits an explicit RETIRE step: the plan states the winner publishes via os.replace and losers poll, but never says whether/when the sibling lock directory created by os.mkdir is removed, nor what a loser does if the lock is released without an artifact ever being published (winner errored after mkdir-release but before publish).
findings.location: Approach — 'Mutual exclusion uses os.mkdir on a sibling lock directory'
scenarios: Winner acquires lock, throws mid-render, process exits leaving the mkdir dir behind — losers correctly fall through at 600s (covered)
Winner releases lock via rmdir on error path but never published — a polling loser sees neither lock nor artifact and must decide to re-acquire
findings.suggested_fix: State that the winner removes the lock directory in a finally block after os.replace (or on error), and that a loser observing neither lock nor artifact re-enters the mkdir acquisition loop rather than assuming a completed render.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Publish the shared render artifact via `rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write` (a stdlib-only leaf module tests already import) rather than a hand-rolled `os.replace`, or justify why the bare rename is preferred over the existing consolidated helper.
evidence: fsutil.py:1 docstring: 'Atomic file writes: temp-in-same-dir + os.replace ... It consolidates the many inline "write a temp file, then rename it over the target" sites ... behind one call'
fsutil.py:3-8: 'Leaf module — stdlib only, NO rebar.* imports — so any layer can depend on it'
tests already use it: test_push_pending_marker.py:228 monkeypatches rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write; test_cache_gitignored.py:12 references the fsutil.atomic_write temp shape
resolve_symbol confirms rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write is importable
findings.finding: The plan hand-rolls the atomic publish via a bare `os.replace`, but the repo already has `rebar._store.fsutil.atomic_write` — a deliberately leaf, stdlib-only module (its docstring: 'NO rebar.* imports, so any layer can depend on it') built to consolidate exactly the 'temp-in-same-dir + os.replace' pattern, and tests already import/monkeypatch it (tests/unit/test_push_pending_marker.py:228, tests/interfaces/store/test_cache_gitignored.py:12). Reusing it gives the mkstemp O_EXCL unique-name + same-dir-fs guarantees that matter under the concurrent-worker race this plan introduces, instead of re-deriving the temp-write-then-rename dance inline.
findings.location: Approach — 'the winner renders and publishes via `os.replace` (atomic, so a visible artifact is always complete)'
scenarios: A winner worker writes the render artifact; if the temp name is not uniquely allocated (mkstemp/O_EXCL) or lands on a different fs than the target, the os.replace is not the intended atomic same-fs rename and a loser can observe a torn file.
findings.suggested_fix: Import `atomic_write` from `rebar._store.fsutil` and use `atomic_write(artifact_path, payload, mode="wb")` for the winner's publish step; it already implements the mkstemp+O_EXCL temp in the same directory and the atomic os.replace.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm render_markdown_to_wiki's rendering logic is fully contained in wiki_render.py, or extend the digest to cover the transitive module sources the render depends on, so a renderer-dependency edit invalidates the cache.
evidence: Plan: 'The artifact filename embeds a SHA-256 digest of ... the wiki_render module source ...'
wiki_render.py imports/uses helpers (e.g. _lock_and_split, _render_unit at lines 150/186) — rendering logic may span more than the single module file
ABSENCE: the plan does not state that render_markdown_to_wiki's full transitive source is self-contained in wiki_render.py
findings.finding: The digest pins only the wiki_render module's own source bytes, but render_markdown_to_wiki's behavior can depend on helper modules it imports (transitive rendering logic); an edit confined to such a dependency would not change the digest and could serve a stale cached render.
findings.location: Approach section — digest bullet ('a SHA-256 digest of the three corpus JSON files, the wiki_render module source, and the resolved pandoc executable path + size')
scenarios: A renderer refactor moves logic into a sibling helper module and edits only that helper; the digest is unchanged and a stale render is served, silently weakening the safety assertions

findings.checklist_item: Justify why a hand-rolled os.mkdir lock + 600s deadline is preferable to filelock.FileLock (already installed and used by the official pytest-xdist recipe), or adopt FileLock.
evidence: Plan quote: 'Mutual exclusion uses `os.mkdir` on a sibling lock directory (atomic on POSIX, no new dependency)'
Plan quote: 'If the lock is held past a 600s deadline the loser renders locally rather than hang' — a bespoke stale-lock/timeout path that filelock provides natively
resolve_symbol: 'filelock.FileLock resolves in the installed environment [third-party (site-packages)]' — the claimed 'no new dependency' benefit is already satisfied by the established primitive
Official pytest-xdist how-to (pytest-xdist.readthedocs.io) uses `from filelock import FileLock` around `tmp_path_factory.getbasetemp().parent` for this exact shared-fixture case
findings.finding: The plan hand-rolls an os.mkdir lock directory with a bespoke 600s poll deadline, justifying it as 'no new dependency' — but filelock.FileLock (the primitive the official pytest-xdist recipe uses for exactly this) is already installed in the environment, so the reinvention is not justified by dependency avoidance.
findings.location: Approach — 'Mutual exclusion uses os.mkdir on a sibling lock directory (atomic on POSIX, no new dependency)'
scenarios: A crashed/hung winner: the hand-rolled 600s deadline degrades to local render, whereas filelock offers timeout + stale-lock handling that is tested across platforms
Non-POSIX runners or future CI platform changes where os.mkdir lock semantics differ from filelock's abstraction
findings.suggested_fix: Use `filelock.FileLock` (already in site-packages) around the shared-artifact publish/read, per the documented pytest-xdist recipe, dropping the bespoke os.mkdir lock and 600s poll loop; retain os.replace for atomic publish.

findings.checklist_item: Cite the official pytest-xdist session-fixture recipe (getbasetemp().parent) the design follows, and note/justify the divergences (unconditional .parent, no worker_id=='master' branch, custom lock).
evidence: Plan quote: 'resolves the shared directory as `tmp_path_factory.getbasetemp().parent`. Under xdist a worker's basetemp is `pytest-<N>/popen-gw<K>`, so `.parent` is `pytest-<N>`' — verbatim the mechanism in the pytest-xdist how-to

Official pytest-xdist how-to shows the same fixture branching on `worker_id == 'master'` for the no-xdist path before using `getbasetemp().parent`; the plan uses `.parent` unconditionally and does not reference the recipe
Prior art exists as a packaged generalization: pytest-shared-session-scope (PyPI) implements this same guide
findings.finding: The Approach reproduces the official pytest-xdist cross-worker session-fixture recipe (getbasetemp().parent shared dir, winner-produces/losers-read) but never cites it or acknowledges the established pattern it derives from, and omits the recipe's worker_id=='master' serial-run branch.
findings.location: Approach — 'A session-scoped fixture corpus_pass1 resolves the shared directory as tmp_path_factory.getbasetemp().parent'
scenarios: Reviewer/maintainer cannot tell the design is the documented xdist pattern and must re-derive its correctness from scratch
Serial (no-xdist / master) run behavior differs from the reference recipe's worker_id branch without the divergence being explained
